description:
⏱️ **Three already-green branches took over two hours to merge, and nothing was wrong with any of them.** Measured on cuneiform 2026-08-21, a `-p1` run at 2h11m: `353-console-linear-order` merged after **~34 minutes** — a branch that was 4/4 and had been verified GREEN before the run started. `355-multimodal-ingest` sat at 3/3 with **2 merge-phase verifies and 6 agent iterations**; `363-composer-stop-control` at 3/3 with another. The operator's summary: *"it takes hours and hours to simply complete one single tasklist. Other projects are not like this."*

**Re-verification after a rebase is CORRECT and this tasklist does not remove it.** `engine/driver.sh`'s own header states the reason: a branch is *"REBASED onto the latest main and RE-VERIFIED (verify_branch). File overlap surfaces as a rebase conflict; semantic staleness surfaces as a verify [failure]... There is no correctness knob to get wrong."* That is right, and this repo has paid for the alternative.

**What is wasted is verifying a tree that DID NOT CHANGE.** There is no verify-result cache anywhere — `GATE_EXIT`/tree-sha caching appears **0 times** in `engine/driver.sh`. So a rebase that is a fast-forward, or that replays to a byte-identical tree, pays a full gate to re-derive a verdict that provably still holds. On cuneiform a full umbrella gate spans go + desktop + engine; the engine arm alone is the long pole.

**Three multipliers stack on top, and together they are the hours.** (1) The AGENT runs its own full `.chief/verify.sh` to decide a story is done, then chief runs the merge-phase gate again — the same tree, twice, by two different callers. (2) An overlap-zone `review` hold parks the branch until `chief approve`, and **approval does not merge** — `chief approve --list` says *"the next run merges it"* — so landing it costs a SECOND run, which rebases onto a main that has since moved and verifies a THIRD time. (3) Merges are serialized on the merge lock, so each branch in a batch rebases onto the previous one's merge and re-verifies; N green branches cost N sequential gates, not one.

**And the operator cannot see any of it.** `chief ps` reported `verifying for 10m` for a branch whose state was `awaiting-approval` — the opposite condition. That single mislabel cost an hour of waiting for something that was waiting on a human. `chief approve --list` had the truth (`state awaiting-approval`) the whole time.

userStories.title: An unchanged tree is not re-verified
userStories.description: The one safe reduction. A rebase that produces a tree identical to the one already verified cannot have changed the verdict, so re-deriving it is pure cost.
acceptanceCriteria: A verify verdict is recorded against the TREE it was computed on (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`, not the commit sha — a rebase rewrites commit shas while leaving the tree identical, which is exactly the case worth catching), together with the base it was verified against and the gate's exit status

When a branch reaches the merge phase and its post-rebase tree matches a recorded GREEN verdict for the same base, the gate is SKIPPED and the run says so — naming the tree and where the verdict came from, so a reader can tell a skip from a pass

Any difference re-verifies: a different tree, a different base, a non-green prior verdict, or no record at all. The cache is an optimisation over an unchanged input and must never be the reason a real failure is missed

The record is per-repo and BOUNDED, and is invalidated when `.chief/verify.sh` itself changes — a verdict computed by a different gate is not a verdict about this one. That file's own mtime/sha is part of the key

Mutation-check it: change one byte in the tree and confirm the gate RUNS; change the gate script and confirm it runs; leave both identical and confirm it skips. A cache that cannot be shown to miss is not safe to trust
userStories.notes: Mutation probe green: identical tree/base/hook skipped with tree SHA and cache path reported; committed tree and verify-hook changes missed and reran. bash -n, quality ratchet, doc-sync, and test/version-bump green; VERSION 0.8.82; shellcheck unavailable.

userStories.title: `chief ps` never reports a waiting branch as working
userStories.description: The mislabel that cost an hour. The state was `awaiting-approval` and the display said `verifying`.
acceptanceCriteria: A branch held at an overlap zone reports a state that names the hold and the action — `awaiting-approval`, with the `chief approve <name>` invocation — in `chief ps`, not only in `chief approve --list`. `ps` is the view an operator watches; a hold invisible there is a hold nobody clears

The phase shown is the phase the branch is IN. `verifying` is never displayed for a branch that is not running a gate, and a test asserts the specific regression: a branch parked at a review zone renders as awaiting approval, never as verifying
The elapsed timer reflects how long it has been WAITING, so `held 2h21m` reads as a queue age rather than as work in progress

`chief ps` states plainly that approval alone does not merge, wherever it shows an approved-but-unmerged branch — the current `--list` wording (*"the next run merges it"*) is correct and is simply not where anyone is looking

userStories.title: Approving a held branch does not require a whole second run to land it
userStories.description: The third gate per branch comes from the approve→run→rebase→re-verify round trip, on a main that moved while the branch was parked.
acceptanceCriteria: An APPROVED branch is merged by the run that is already in flight when approval happens, if one is — rather than requiring a fresh `chief run` naming it. The round trip is what forces the extra rebase and the third gate

If no run is in flight, `chief approve` states the exact command that will land it, so the two-step is explicit rather than discovered. Silence after an approval is the current behaviour and it reads as done

A branch approved and then merged in the same run is verified ONCE if its tree did not change (US-1's cache is what makes this true) — the acceptance is on the observable gate count for a batch of N approved green branches, which must not be N gates when nothing moved between them
Nothing here weakens the zone. A `review` zone still holds until a human approves, however green the gate came back; this story changes only what happens AFTER the human says yes

userStories.title: The agent's own verify and the merge gate are not two full runs of the same thing
userStories.description: An agent runs `.chief/verify.sh` to decide a story is done; chief then runs it again at merge. Same script, same tree, two callers.
acceptanceCriteria: An agent-side verify records its verdict in the same tree-keyed store US-1 introduces, so the merge phase can reuse it when the tree is unchanged rather than re-running the identical gate
The agent's verify remains available and unchanged in behaviour — it is how a story is decided, and removing it would make the agent guess. This story removes the DUPLICATION, not the check
The measured outcome is stated in the notes: for a tasklist that finishes green with no rebase, the number of full gate executions between the agent's decision and the merge drops from two to one
A tree that DID change between the agent's verdict and the merge still verifies at merge — the common case of an agent committing after its own verify must not be optimised into a skip
